headline: Backup Report for Travis County Homes
summary: Homes in Travis County face an elevated risk. Long outages of 12 hours or more happen about once every 8 years (fact: outlook.once_every_years). This comes from 8 years of records since 2018 (fact: outlook.years_of_data). In February 2021, 43% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth went without power for about 74 hours (fact: event.1.p90_hours). In February 2023, 29% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth went without power for about 106 hours (fact: event.2.p90_hours). One Core lasts about 14 hours in August (fact: backup.short_month). One Core lasts about 30 hours in February (fact: backup.long_month). Two Cores are suggested for a home with gas heat and a larger footprint (fact: sizing.cores). Two Cores cover 78% of past 12-hour-plus outage hours (fact: sizing.share). Base confirms sizing at install.
